_doc: VIEW-STATE family (VIEWSEED, 2026-07-27). The first fixtures anywhere in
test_fixtures/ that set zoom_level / view_offset — every other case in the
corpus runs at the IDENTITY view, where screen<->document conversion is
algebraically the identity and therefore cannot fail. See
transcripts/CORPUS_CENSUS.md 5.7 and the `identity-view-only` row in
scripts/corpus_manifest.json.
Each case seeds the per-tab view through the new `view` block
{zoom_level, view_offset_x, view_offset_y, viewport_w, viewport_h} and
asserts the resulting triple through `expected_view`. The document golden
is asserted too and is the UNCHANGED two_rects import: a view action must
not touch document content, and pinning that is half the value of the
family.
GOLDENS ARE SPEC-DERIVED, NOT PORT-CAPTURED. Every expected_view triple
below is the transcripts/ZOOM_TOOL.md 'Anchor and clamp math' block
evaluated in IEEE-754 double by a third implementation (CPython), then
checked against both ports:
doc_ax = (ax - px) / z ; doc_ay = (ay - py) / z
z_new  = clamp(z * f, min_zoom, max_zoom)
px_new = ax - doc_ax * z_new ; py_new = ay - doc_ay * z_new
and, for the fit_* verbs, the same file's zoom_fit_rect primitive:
z = clamp(min((vw - 2*pad)/w, (vh - 2*pad)/h), min_zoom, max_zoom)
px = vw/2 - (x + w/2)*z ; py = vh/2 - (y + h/2)*z
The long decimals are exact double results, not rounded transcriptions.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: the two default-anchor verbs. zoom_in /
zoom_out with no anchor params, and zoom_to_actual_size, are LIVE
DIVERGENCES between the ports at this commit and each fix lands in a file
reserved by a concurrent wave. Both are written out, with their
spec-derived triples and the observed per-port outputs, in the
`view-anchor-default-divergence` and `view-zoom-set-pan-divergence` rows of
scripts/corpus_manifest.json coverage_gaps. Pinning either one here today
would red a lane; pinning a port's current output instead would be a test
whose expected value coincides with the bug.
name: zoom_in_explicit_anchor

_doc: The reciprocal factor (1.0 / zoom_step). Same anchor, same seed, so the
pair brackets the anchor algebra in both directions; the ugly decimals are
what the formula actually produces at f = 1/1.2 and are bit-identical in
both ports (the literals below are shortest-round-trip forms).
name: zoom_out_explicit_anchor

_doc: AT-CLAMP anchor stability. z = 60 with zoom_step 1.2 asks for 72; the
clamp caps it at max_zoom = 64. ZOOM_TOOL.md requires the ACTUALLY APPLIED
factor to drive the pan recompute, so the document point under (300, 200)
must still be under (300, 200) afterwards. A port that panned with the
requested 72 instead would land at px = -400 rather than -126.67, i.e. the
canvas would jump at the zoom limit.
name: zoom_in_clamped_at_max_zoom

_doc: The min_zoom mirror: already at 0.1, a zoom_out is a silent no-op in BOTH
coordinates. Note the pan is unchanged only because the applied factor is
1.0 after clamping — the effect still runs the full anchor recompute, so a
port that clamped zoom but not the pan factor would move the offsets here.
name: zoom_out_clamped_at_min_zoom

_doc: Two step zooms in a row from a NON-identity seed, anchored at two
different points. The single-action cases above cannot see a port that
reads the view from a stale snapshot instead of the live model, because
one action has nothing to be stale against. Derived by applying the anchor
on x is genuine — it is what the formula's exact double arithmetic
produces — and pinning it rather than a rounded -316 is deliberate: the
two ports must agree bit for bit, not to within a tolerance.
name: zoom_in_twice_moving_anchor

_doc: fit_in_window over the element bounding box, from a seed that is wrong in
BOTH zoom and pan so neither can be inherited. two_rects.svg imports at the
0.75 px->pt scale, so the two 96x96 rects occupy doc 0..144 x 0..72. The
fit is the zoom_fit_rect primitive with padding = fit_padding_px, whose
declared default in workspace/preferences.yaml is 20. That the effect arg
'preferences.viewport.fit_padding_px' RESOLVES (rather than evaluating to
0, which several sibling effects fall back to for min_zoom / max_zoom) is
itself pinned here: at padding 0 the triple would be
name: fit_in_window_from_wrong_view

_doc: fit_all_artboards over the UNION of the document's artboards, which is a
different rect from the element bbox the previous case fits — the whole
distinction actions.yaml draws between the three fit verbs. The setup
changes to two_artboards.svg (misnamed upstream: it declares THREE pages,
at x = 0, 120, 240, each 96x96, importing at the 0.75 px->pt scale to
doc 0..252 x 0..72) because an SVG without <inkscape:page> elements
imports with an EMPTY artboards list, and on an empty list this effect is
an early-return no-op in both ports. That no-op is real but it is a
property of the fixture, not of the verb, and a vector that asserts
'nothing happened' would pass in a port that never implemented the verb.
name: fit_all_artboards_from_wrong_view

_doc: fit_active_artboard resolves ONE artboard rather than the union, through
'active_document.current_artboard.{x,y,width,height}' in actions.yaml. With
no panel selection the current artboard is the first (ARTBOARDS.md
§Selection semantics), so this fits the 0..72 x 0..72 board and lands at a
different zoom from the union case above — which is what separates it from
fit_all_artboards. It also gates the scope plumbing: a port whose action
dispatch does not publish active_document.current_artboard resolves all
four args to 0 and the effect early-returns on w <= 0, leaving the seeded
NOT COVERED: the same verb with the SECOND artboard panel-selected, which
is where the census's row #8 puts a divergence. The action fixture format
has no way to express a panel selection — see the
`view-current-artboard-panel-selection` coverage-gap row.
name: fit_active_artboard_from_wrong_view

_doc: ZOOMPKG (2026-07-27). The DEFAULT-ANCHOR vectors. These were deliberately
absent when the family was seeded: the `view-anchor-default-divergence`
coverage-gap row recorded that zoom_in / zoom_out with NO anchor params
anchored at the viewport centre in Rust and at the doc origin's screen
position in Swift, and that pinning the spec value would red the swift
lane. JYH RULED 2026-07-27 that the viewport centre is the requirement
(transcripts/ZOOM_TOOL.md, the ruling headed 'the DEFAULT ZOOM ANCHOR is
the viewport centre'), Swift was fixed in the same wave as this vector,
and that gap row is now closed.
TWO causes had to land together for this vector to pass, which is why it
could not be pinned earlier as a half-fix:
(a) the dispatcher must merge the action's DECLARED param defaults, so
`param.anchor_x` resolves to actions.yaml's -1 rather than null->0;
(b) doc.zoom.apply must have a viewport-centre branch for that -1
sentinel. Swift had NEITHER; it carried viewportW and never read it.
Fixing only (a) lands at (-100, -50); only (b) lands at (-120, -60); the
golden below is reached by both together. So this vector discriminates
three ways and its expected value coincides with no partial fix.
GOLDEN, spec-derived (the 'Anchor and clamp math' block of ZOOM_TOOL.md
with ax = viewport_w / 2, ay = viewport_h / 2):
name: zoom_in_default_anchor

_doc: The zoom_out half of the default-anchor pair. Same seed, same anchor rule,
factor 1/1.2. Both offsets move AWAY from the seed and view_offset_y
changes SIGN (-50 -> +8.33...), which neither a pan-unchanged nor an
origin-anchored implementation produces, so this is not a value a wrong
port reaches by luck.
Exact double results, not rounded transcriptions:
name: zoom_out_default_anchor

_doc: The UNMEASURED-VIEWPORT fallback of the default anchor. Both ports fall
back to the doc origin's screen position (px, py) when viewport_w /
viewport_h are still 0 -- the state before the canvas widget has reported
its size. This is the one case where the pre-ruling Swift output was
already right, so the fallback is PINNED rather than deleted, and this is
the vector that catches a 'fix' that divides into a zero viewport.
ax=px=-100 ; ay=py=-50 ; doc_ax=doc_ay=0 ; z_new=2.4 ; pan unchanged
name: zoom_in_default_anchor_unmeasured_viewport

_doc: ZOOMPKG (2026-07-27). zoom_to_actual_size RECENTRES on the viewport
centre. Also deliberately absent when the family was seeded: the
`view-zoom-set-pan-divergence` gap row recorded Swift leaving the pan
alone and Rust recentring, and -- correctly at the time -- that the
WRITTEN SPEC sided with Swift. JYH RULED 2026-07-27 that the spec was
wrong in four places and Rust was right (transcripts/ZOOM_TOOL.md, the
ruling headed 'zoom_to_actual_size RECENTRES'). Those four statements plus
ZOOM_TOOL_TESTS.md's ZOOM-134 parenthetical were rewritten in the same
wave as this vector, and that gap row is now closed.
Why 'pan unchanged' was the wrong requirement: view_offset is the DOC
ORIGIN's screen position, so holding it fixed while zoom goes 4x -> 1x
quadruples the visible region around that point. At the seed below the
and the artwork leaves the screen.
GOLDEN, spec-derived (the doc point under the viewport centre is held):
The invariant that encodes: (400-225)/1 == 175 == doc_cx and
(300-175)/1 == 125 == doc_cy -- the artist keeps looking at doc
name: zoom_to_actual_size_recentres

_doc: The UNMEASURED-VIEWPORT fallback of zoom_to_actual_size: with viewport_w
/ viewport_h at 0 there is no centre to anchor on, so both ports write
zoom_level and leave the pan literally unchanged. Pins the guard that
keeps the recentre from dividing into an unmeasured viewport, and is the
only vector in this family where 'pan unchanged' is still the right
answer.
name: zoom_to_actual_size_unmeasured_viewport
